newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 22.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following a heated five-hour annual meeting, which resulted in a fierce battle to oust steel pipe millionaire Ross Palmer from the Australian National Industries board, long-standing ANI director Peter Joseph appeared to have held on to his position. It was the climax of an irreconcilable board split triggered by the group's disastrous investment in German environmental engineering group Holter. Page 1.

In talks with Resources and Energy Minister Warwick Parer in Japan early this month, Japanese companies said growth in the APEC region would enhance Australia's status as a reliable supplier of food and fuels, but some expressed concern over Australia's industrial relations and environmental and export controls. Page 3.

Two of Australia's leading competition experts, Professor Fred Hilmer and Industry Commission chairman Bill Scales, have called for a relaxation of the nation's tough merger laws. Scales told a Metal Trades Industry Association Forum in Canberra yesterda that some of Australia's merger regulation was "unnecessary" and Hilmer said Australia was disadvantaged by only having 16 large businesses with an average worth of A$4 billion. Page 3.

Former Woolworths chairman Paul Simons told a joint meeting of the Japan-Australia and Australia-Japan Business Cooperation Committees in Sydney yesterday that restructuring in the Japanese retail and wholesale sectors has made it much easier for exporter to access the market, with many opportunities for niche retailing. Page 3.

Brewing analysts have estimated that Canadian brewer Molson will have to pay US brewer Coors in excess of A$20 million following an independent panel's ruling that Molson had breached a licensing agreement. Forty per cent owned by Foster's Brewing Group Ltd, Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel said it was too early to assess the financial ramifications of the Molson ruling. Page 21.

Australia's brokers are split in their views on BHP Co Ltd, with a report from Macquarie Equities analyst Greg Yeatman suggesting a 12-month share price outlook of about A$14.30, recommending shareholders quit the stock, while Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd suggsts that BHP will outperform the sharemarket over the next year. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following a highly charged five-hour annual meeting of about 700 shareholders in Sydney last night, which saw Australian National Industries inundated with questions from disgruntled shareholders, Ross Palmer was removed from the ANI board. Page 19.

In a move that signals a dramatic downgrading of RTZ-CRA's research into aluminium, the group yesterday slashed up to 70 jobs from research and development centres in Melbourne and Perth. The cutbacks are expected to cut an estimated A$20 million from RTZ-CRA's global R&D budget of A$130 million. Page 19.

According to a paper delivered by Minoru Inouye, an adviser to the Bank of Tokyo, to the joint meeting of the Australia-Japan Business Co-operation meeting yesterday, Japanese investment in Australia increased by 91.5 per cent over 1994 and is continuing to increase and diversify away from its historic reliance on resources and into manufacturing. Page 19.

Coles Myer chairman Nobby Clark, fresh from announcing a restructure of the Coles board on Friday, revealed yesterday Solomon Lew would not be called on to explain to Coles shareholders his role in the controversial 1991 Yannon transaction, which resulted in Coles losing A$18 million before recovering A$12 million in a mediated settlement last August. Page 19.

Struggling pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd is maintaining a strict media silence on the progress of its A$190 million bond issue in the US, with interim managing director Larry Carleton saying he was unaware of the progress of the issue. However, it s believed Australis is still trying to secure the price and yield of its secured discount notes. Page 21.

BHP chairman-elect Jerry Ellis has warned that for Australia to be able to succeed in "this ferociously competitive world", the Federal Government must "maintain and raise the pace" of structural reform and eliminate impediments to competition. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian National Industries' boardroom brawl appeared to have been resolved yesterday, with institutional shareholders voting during a heated five-hour annual general meeting to drop dissident director Ross Palmer from the ANI board in favour of fellow director Peter Joseph. Page 25.

In a transaction which ignited speculation National Australia Bank is building a stake in Westpac Banking Corp ahead of the Wallis inquiry, which could allow big bank mergers, a mystery buyer spent more than A$90 million just before the close of trading lst night to pick up 11 million Westpac convertible preference shares. Page 25.

Due largely to a doubling in revenue from A$19.6 million to A$39 million, Aussie Home Loans, the leader of the new school of cut-price home lenders, has recorded a sevenfold increase in pre-tax profit for 1995-96, to A$4.52 million for the year to June 30 and has flagged moves to become a fully-rounded financial service provider. Page 25.

The author of Australia's competition policy, Professor Fred Hilmer, and Productivity Commission head Bill Scales both claimed yesterday Australian firms are being restricted in the global marketplace by the tight grip of the Australian Competition and Cosumer Commission on mergers. Page 27.

Entrepreneur Albert Hadid launched the first stage of his A$400 million damages claim against pay-TV operator Australis Media yesterday - Hadid is suing Australis for A$158 million over an alleged verbal agreement struck during the auctioning by the Goverment of six microwave licences - claiming Australis reneged on a deal to deliver two of the licenses. Page 27.

In a surprise decision, an independent arbitration panel has ruled that Canadian brewer Molson breached its licensing agreement with US brewer Coors and has ordered Molson to pay Coors all profits on the production and sale of Coors brands in Canada since1993 - a move that could hit Foster's Brewing Group's profit contribution from Molson. Page 27.
THE AGE

Following a heated five-hour Australian National Industries annual meeting yesterday, in which small shareholders directed support at both Ross Palmer and Peter Joseph, institutional shareholders held the final sway, voting to dump dissident director Palmer from the board. Page C1.

Strongly denying allegations of evading more than A$50 million in tax, two lawyers from Jerusalem-based News Corp subsidiary News Datacom Research will face questioning today after Sunday's raid on NDR by Income Tax Authority officials. According to tax officials, Rupert Murdoch himself could be questioned if he were to set foot in Israel. Page C1.

Less than three days after the Federal Government's asset sales taskforce short-listed Hudson Conway HDC.AX as a bidder for Melbourne Airport, Hudson Conway chief executive Lloyd Williams announced that the company would not pay above A$1 billion for the airport and he would personally prefer the Docklands project as the company's next big project. Page C1.

The profit contribution from Foster's Brewing Group's Canadian brewer Molson could be hit following an independent panel decision that Molson had breached a licensing agreement with US brewer Coors and must pay Coors all profits on the production and sale of Coors brands in Canada since 1993. Page C1.

Discovery Petroleum has declared Premier Oil's 70 cents-a-share takeover bid neither fair nor reasonable, following a valuation of its shares by Grant Samuel & Associates which valued shares at between 77 cents and 95 cents. Discovery's board has unanimously recommended that shareholders reject the offer. Page C3.

RTZ-CRA will cut 76 jobs in Melbourne associated with the research and development effort of its aluminium subsidiary Comalco, after a review of the group's R&D activities identified an annual saving of about A$20 million on the A$130 million RTZ-CRA currntly spends on R&D in Australia. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
